text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- The newspaper editorial says Albania's economy, dominated by politics, is not the determining factor for the country's life and fate.
- The opposition Socialists have opposed the Central Electoral Commission on the age-limit for election observers. They have asked the Constitutional Court to make a final ruling.
- A newspaper commentary denounces the prime minister for telling voters in the capital to vote for the Democratic Party if they want the government to help Tirana.
- The foreign ministry will reshuffle some 40 percent of its staff, including its embassies in EU member countries.
- The consumer price index for September was 2.5 percent higher and the annual index 17.7 percent higher, according to the latest figures from the Institute of Statistics.
- Siemens has started the reconstruction of Rinasi international airport, for which a German government soft credit of 48 million marks will be used.
- Despite the start of the Albania's mass immunisation programme against polio other patients infected with the virus have been admitted to hospital.
- Foreigners love marrying Albanian women because they are calm, loyal and cook well, the newspaper says.
- Albanian novelist Ismail Kadare became a member of the French Academy.
- Albania failed its first test in the World Cup soccer qualifiers, beaten by Portugal 3-0 in a group nine match.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Companies organising pyramide schemes have increased monthly interest payments to reassure Albanians they will get back their money.
- A policeman was killed in the northern city of Shkoder but investigators do not know who was responsible.
- Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi has rejected a Socialist accusation that Albania's ruling party illegally used part of the government's 1996 budget in its election campaign.
- The Republican candidate for the post of Tirana mayor has asked his rivals to enter a television debate.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Tritan Shehu, deputy prime minister, foreign minister and chairman of the Democratic Party, left for Britain to participate in the convention of the Conservative Party of Prime Minister John Major.
- President Sali Berisha continued meetings in south-western Albania, introducing ruling party candidates for October 20 local elections.
